response_text: Reducing the OS clock tick interval from 1 ms to 0.1 ms means the system can perform finer-grained time slicing, which allows for more responsive multitasking. This is especially beneficial for real-time systems requiring high-frequency updates or very short response times. However, the downside is increased overhead. A timer interrupt will now occur 10 times more often, increasing the number of context switches and reducing the CPU time available for actual thread execution. It also consumes more power and can lead to timing jitter or missed deadlines if the system cannot handle the increased interrupt load efficiently.\n
